cf.title: Remove invalid SS2/SS3 handling from EUC-KR routines

input.subject: Remove invalid SS2/SS3 handling from EUC-KR routines

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived the critic. The only one raised, demand-1, was refuted: the new width estimates match the true 2-byte maximum of EUC_KR, and the effects reach only EUC_KR databases on master. The patch aligns mblen, dsplen and maxmblen with KS X 2901 and with pg_euckr_verifychar(). Confidence is medium because no one has replied to v4 and two points could not be checked without the code.

brief.title: Remove SS2/SS3 handling from EUC-KR encoding routines
brief.problem: EUC-KR, per KS X 2901, has only ASCII and KS X 1001, so SS2 (0x8E) and SS3 (0x8F) are never valid lead bytes. Postgres still routes EUC-KR mblen, dsplen and mb2wchar through the shared pg_euc_* helpers, which handle SS2/SS3, and the docs list 1-3 bytes per character. The verifier already rejects these bytes, so the code and the docs disagree with it.
brief.proposed_design: The patch replaces pg_euckr_mblen(), pg_euckr_dsplen() and pg_euckr2wchar_with_len() with EUC-KR-only versions that know 1-byte and 2-byte sequences, like UHC. It lowers maxmblen for EUC_KR from 3 to 2 and fixes the charset table to "1-2". v4 is split: 0001 adds tests that record current behavior, 0002 makes the change.
user_visible_surface: In EUC_KR databases, the planner's width estimates for char(n) and varchar(n) shrink, for example from 34 to 24 for char(10).
A new table whose columns all have a bounded width may no longer get a TOAST table, for example one varchar(700) column.
Invalid-byte-sequence errors starting with 0x8F show two bytes instead of three.
The Bytes/Char entry for EUC_KR in the charset documentation table changes from 1-3 to 1-2.
author_claims: KS X 2901 leaves code sets 2 and 3 undefined, so no valid EUC-KR text contains SS2 or SS3.
Valid EUC-KR data is handled exactly as before, because pg_euckr_verifychar() never admits 0x8E or 0x8F.
Only 0x8F changes length; pg_euc_mblen() already returned 2 for 0x8E.
lpad('x', 400000000) fails on master and succeeds with v4 in EUC_KR databases.
The full parallel_schedule in an EUC_KR database shows only two changed lines, and the change is for master only.
brief.thread_state: Henson Choi reviewed and marked it Ready for Committer, but John Naylor set it back to Waiting on Author for missing tests and showed plan width changes. v4 adds the tests and documents these effects, and no one has replied to v4 yet.
unclear: No reviewer has checked the effect on unverified 0x8F data that is already on disk, for example after pg_upgrade or in shared catalogs.
The thread does not say whether changed TOAST-table creation can affect pg_upgrade or dump and restore of EUC_KR databases.
Michael Paquier's question about src/test/locale/ has an answer from the author but no reply from him.
Henson Choi's review list (P1 to P5) was never reported as completed.
The thread does not say whether anyone considers the plan and TOAST changes acceptable for users of EUC_KR.

refuted.title: No reported user problem to weigh against plan and TOAST changes
refuted.failure_scenario: An EUC_KR site upgrades to version 20. Width estimates for char(n) and varchar(n) drop by about a third, so some plans change. The site finds out from a slower query after the upgrade, and nobody had asked for the change.
refuted.argument: The material contains no field report, -general or -bugs thread, or user request about the EUC_KR maxmblen value. Every effect a user can see is a change: plan widths (message #9), TOAST table creation, the lpad() limit and error text (message #10). The stated gain is agreement with KS X 2901 and the verifier, plus estimates that are closer to the truth, and a committer may accept that. The thread still has no judgement that these changes are acceptable for EUC_KR users.
refuted.author_must_show: Has any EUC_KR user hit a problem with maxmblen = 3, or is there evidence that the new width estimates give better plans for real EUC_KR workloads?

critic.reasoning: The new width estimates match the true 2-byte maximum of EUC_KR, so the scenario of a slower query is speculative. The effects reach only EUC_KR databases, are listed in the v4 commit message, and are limited to master, where planner estimates change in every major release.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: New tables with bounded-width columns may no longer get a TOAST table, and unverified 0x8F text on disk splits differently.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: pg_wchar_table[PG_EUC_KR].maxmblen in src/common/wchar.c drops from 3 to 2, which extensions and frontend code can read.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: Width estimates for char(n) and varchar(n) shrink in EUC_KR databases, for example from 34 to 24 for char(10).

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: A restored table in an EUC_KR database may get no TOAST table where the old cluster had one.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The patch changes character length and buffer sizing rules in wchar.c, an area with a recent CVE fix for EUC_CN.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Three EUC-KR-specific routines replace calls to the shared pg_euc_* helpers, in the same shape as UHC.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Does pg_upgrade in binary-upgrade mode still create the TOAST table for an EUC_KR table that had one in the old cluster but would not get one under maxmblen = 2?
How do the new routines split unverified text containing 0x8F that is already on disk, such as shared catalog names written from a database with another encoding?
Does any reader of mblen or maxmblen for EUC_KR still assume a 3-byte maximum after the change?
Were the checks P1 to P5 in Henson Choi's review list completed against v4?
Is src/test/locale/ affected by the change, as Michael Paquier asked in message #3?

committability.owner_note: John Naylor reviewed the patch, showed the plan width changes and set the status; Michael Paquier asked for tests. The owner needs to know the multibyte encoding code in wchar.c.
committability.liability: The owner signs for EUC_KR length handling in wchar.c, for the plan and TOAST-table changes in EUC_KR databases after upgrade to version 20, and for any reader of unverified 0x8F data that behaves differently.
committability.author_follow_up: The author produced v4 with the requested tests and a commit message that lists the user-visible effects, about a month after the status was set back to Waiting on Author.

priority.reason: The change affects only EUC_KR databases, adds no new mechanism, and the 0002 patch is about 6.5 KB in wchar.c plus docs and tests. v4 answers the reviewers' requests and waits for a reply.

provisional_note: Without the code, two points could not be checked: whether pg_upgrade keeps existing TOAST tables for EUC_KR tables under the new size rule, and whether each reader of mblen and maxmblen is safe with unverified 0x8F bytes.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Encoding protection for pgcrypto
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pgp_sym_decrypt_text and pgp_pub_decrypt_text check that the decrypted result is valid in the database encoding, and raise an error if it is not. It adds regression tests for this and moves some existing tests that failed under some encodings.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Cary Huang reported failing tests and questioned aborting the transaction instead of issuing a warning. The author posted v2 and argued that callers who want no encoding check can use the bytea variants, and no later message follows.

precedents_retrieved.title: Clarify the comments about varlena header encoding
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch rewrites the comments in postgres.h that describe the bit layouts of varlena headers, so readers do not misread the length word, the alignment notes or the size of a TOAST pointer. Version 2 adds a 0b prefix to the bit patterns and mentions the type tag next to the TOAST pointer layout.
precedents_retrieved.objection: John Naylor found that both versions made the comments harder to read. In his view, adding the type tag pulls the comment away from its purpose, which is to show how the first byte tells what kind of varlena follows. He judged the current text a local maximum that small edits would likely make worse, and doubted that any change was needed. The author did not reply for four weeks, so Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
More broadly, I think the description of varlenas in this header is at
a kind of "local maximum" -- minor adjustments are more likely to make
it worse.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add uri percent-encoding for binary data
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds 'uri' as a format for encode() and decode(), using RFC 3986 percent-encoding on binary data. The author wanted fast URL building in PL/pgSQL, for example with encode(convert_to(..., 'UTF8'), 'uri').
precedents_retrieved.objection: Daniel Gustafsson argued that the encoding ignores the URI scheme and context, so it percent-encodes delimiters such as those in https:// and the @ in userinfo, and double-encodes IPv6 zone identifiers. He suggested renaming it to 'percent-encoding' instead. The author did not send a new version addressing this feedback, and the patch no longer applied, so the entry was closed at the end of July 2020.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I agree that uri decoding/encoding would be useful, but I'm not convinced that
this patch does the functionality justice enough to be useful.

precedents_retrieved.title: Nonreplayable XLog records by means of overflows and >MaxAllocSize lengths
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds checks in xloginsert.c so that the WAL insertion API cannot assemble a record larger than xlogreader can read (MaxAllocSize, later a fixed 1020 MiB limit), and cannot overflow xl_tot_len through repeated XLogRegisterData() calls. It also documents the record size limit in the XLogRecord spec.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier committed part of the patch, the API changes and the uint16 block data checks. He then asked for a rebase of the rest, and the author did not reply for two commitfests, so the entry was returned with feedback. After it was closed, Andres Freund noted that the new record-too-large ERROR usually happens inside a critical section and so becomes a PANIC. He suggested building large records such as the commit record before the critical section.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
No replies after 4 weeks, so I have marked this entry as returned
with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch computes the lengths of the 'passwd' and 'secret' strings once at the start of PerformRadiusTransaction. This removes repeated strlen() calls inside its loops.

precedents_retrieved.title: Defend against encoding ID version skew
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch renames the encoding functions that libpq exports (pg_char_to_encoding, pg_valid_server_encoding_id and related ones) so that they differ from the libpgcommon copies, and each caller links to a known copy regardless of link order. initdb then uses the backend's encoding IDs and psql uses libpq's, which defends against version skew with a libpq from another release.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. In the last messages Tom Lane posts v2 with meson support and plans to push it, and Andres Freund agrees with the plan, raising only a minor meson point about c_args.

precedents_retrieved.title: hstore: add hstore_length(hstore) function
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an hstore_length(hstore) function to contrib/hstore that returns HS_COUNT, the number of key/value pairs. It also adds documentation, upgrade SQL files and tests, so users no longer need to convert an hstore to an array to count its pairs.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch did not apply against master. The reviewer also asked to drop the HSTORE_POLLUTE line for the new function and to use uint32 with PG_RETURN_UINT32 for the count. No reply from the author appears in the visible messages, and the entry was returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add test module for verifying backtrace functionality
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds TAP tests that check the backtrace code in elog.c (backtrace_functions, backtrace_on_internal_error, errbacktrace) by looking for "BACKTRACE: " and the failing function name in the server log. It first used a new module, src/test/modules/test_backtrace, and later moved the test to src/test/modules/test_misc.

roaster_notes.note: The precedent search found no earlier proposal with the same or a similar idea. Message #1 points to an earlier discussion and message #8 to related Korean encoding fixes (CF 6913, BUG #19354), but the thread does not report a rejection of either, so no prior reason applies here.

Nothing from the standards and compatibility angle supports rejection. The patch brings mblen, dsplen and maxmblen in line with KS X 2901 and with the existing pg_euckr_verifychar(), which already rejects 0x8E and 0x8F, so no valid EUC_KR text changes meaning. The visible effects are smaller width estimates in plans, fewer TOAST tables for new tables, pg_encoding_max_length('EUC_KR') returning 2, and shorter 0x8F error messages. Message #10 and the 0002 commit message list all of these, and the change targets master only. Without the code I could not check one case: whether pg_upgrade --binary-upgrade still creates a TOAST table for a table that had one in the old cluster but would not get one under the new size rule. A committer would likely want that answered before commit, but the brief gives no concrete failure there.

The patch changes no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, wire message or ABI, and targets master only, so no mixed-version standby or backpatch exists. Valid EUC_KR data is verified on input and splits the same way. Only unverified 0x8F text, mostly shared-catalog names, splits differently, and nothing persisted is derived from that split. The TOAST-table change could not be checked without the code: whether pg_upgrade still carries over existing TOAST tables for EUC_KR tables that would no longer get one.

No privilege, exposure or denial-of-service issue found: no new object, privilege or default, and after the patch no EUC-KR routine treats a character as longer than 2 bytes, so maxmblen and mblen agree. The effect on unverified 0x8F bytes, such as shared catalog text, and on buffer sizing by maxmblen could not be checked without the code.

From the maintenance and fit angle there is no objection. The patch makes EUC-KR's three routines the same shape as UHC's, adds no new mechanism, GUC or API, and costs nothing on a common path. The plan-width and TOAST-table changes fall only on EUC_KR databases, are listed in the commit message, and are for master only. John Naylor, who knows the encoding code, is engaged (message #9), and v4 answers his request for tests. Henson Choi's EUC-CN note (message #2) is a separate follow-up and does not bind the project to anything. Without the code, two things could not be checked: whether each mblen and maxmblen reader is covered, and how unverified 0x8F data already on disk behaves.

Postgres has no existing feature, option or extension that makes the EUC_KR mblen, dsplen and mb2wchar routines match the verifier, or that reports maxmblen 2 for EUC_KR. The patch changes core encoding tables that no extension or hook can reach. It adds no second mechanism and reuses the existing UHC shape.
This is a correctness cleanup, and its costs fall only on EUC_KR databases. The single objection asks for the user-facing benefit to be stated. It is not a reason to reject the patch.
